2027 Budget second reading passed by 97-vote majority

cards.what_happened: Parliament passed the second reading of the 2027 Budget by a 97-vote majority following a seven-day debate. The vote concluded with 157 votes in favour and 60 votes against. This is the 81st Budget in the history of Sri Lanka.
details: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake presented the proposal on November 12 in his role as Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development. Debate began on November 13 and finished at 6.30 pm on November 20, marking the third budget presented by the National People’s Power government. Records show 157 MPs voted in favour, 60 MPs voted against, and no MPs abstained.

The 2027 Budget estimates total government spending at Rs. 7.933 trillion, up from Rs. 7.309 trillion in revised 2026 estimates. Total revenue is projected at Rs. 6.15 trillion, while revenue and grants reach Rs. 6.18 trillion. These figures leave an estimated budget deficit of Rs. 1.753 trillion, representing 4.5% of Gross Domestic Product.

Alongside these proceedings, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe announced headline inflation will likely exceed 9% this month. In judicial matters, Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama ordered a progress report on the Krrish inquiry by December 01, while MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake was further remanded until November 27.
key_facts: The 2027 Budget second reading passed with 157 votes in favour and 60 against.
A 97-vote majority cleared the proposal after a seven-day parliamentary debate.
President Anura Kumara Dissanayake presented the proposal on November 12.
Government expenditure is estimated at Rs. 7.933 trillion for 2027.
Total revenue is projected at Rs. 6.15 trillion, creating a Rs. 1.753 trillion deficit.
Committee Stage discussions run from November 21 until December 14 across 19 days.
The final third reading vote is scheduled for 6.00 pm on December 14.
Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe expects inflation to top 9% this month.
cards.whats_next: The Committee Stage debate begins on November 21 and runs across 19 days until December 14, meeting at 9.30 am each day except Sundays and public holidays, ahead of a final vote at 6.00 pm on December 14.
cards.blurb: Sri Lanka's Parliament has approved the second reading of the 2027 Budget by a 97-vote majority.
cards.spoken: Sri Lanka's Parliament has approved the second reading of the 2027 Budget by a ninety-seven-vote majority. After seven days of debate, one hundred and fifty-seven lawmakers voted in favour, while sixty voted against, with no abstentions. Presented by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake as Finance Minister, this is the eighty-first budget in the country's history. It outlines government spending of seven point nine three three trillion rupees and projects an estimated deficit of one point seven five three trillion rupees. Meanwhile, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe warned that inflation will likely top nine percent this month. Lawmakers now move to the Committee Stage debate, which continues until the final vote on December 14.

Two youths missing after drowning incident in Nintavur

cards.what_happened: Two youths are missing after reportedly drowning while bathing in the sea off Nintavur. A third youth was rescued by local residents and admitted to hospital. The missing youths are aged 16 and 23 and live in Nintavur.
details: Three youths were bathing in the sea off Nintavur when two of them reportedly drowned. Police said local residents rescued one of the three youths and admitted him to hospital.
The missing youths are aged 16 and 23 and are residents of Nintavur. The report comes from Newswire.
Navy divers, local residents and Nintavur Police have launched search operations to locate the missing youths.
key_facts: Two youths are missing after a drowning incident off Nintavur.
The missing youths are aged 16 and 23 and live in Nintavur.
A third youth was rescued by local residents and admitted to hospital.
Police confirmed one of the three youths involved was rescued.
Navy divers, local residents and Nintavur Police are searching for the missing youths.
cards.blurb: Two youths are missing after drowning off Nintavur while a third was rescued and taken to hospital.
cards.spoken: Hello and welcome. A search is under way off Nintavur after two young people went missing while bathing in the sea. Police say there were three youths in the water, and local residents managed to rescue one of them. That person was taken to hospital. The two who are still missing are aged 16 and 23, and both live in Nintavur. Navy divers, local residents and Nintavur Police are all working together to find them. The story comes from Newswire. The article does not say exactly when it happened or what happens next, but the search is ongoing right now.
